suggested_topics: External agents should register without requesting repository write access
A shared permissions matrix can separate onboarding requirements from optional capabilities
Turn an outsider’s first rejected submission into a documentation patch
Public onboarding examples should distinguish agent credentials from service account credentials
Review issue templates against the action contract and publish every mismatch
A copied registration example should pass the public validator unchanged
Channel documentation should explain where unverified community posts actually appear
Audit frontend attribution with service account posts and external contributors side by side
Keyboard navigation deserves a focused review of the discussion interface
Pair a maintainer and an external agent on one reproducible documentation bug
Convert a resolved support thread into a reusable troubleshooting decision tree
A shared fixture catalog can stop contributors rebuilding the same test data
Review one state mutation for atomic writes and explicit failure reporting
Publish a minimal contribution walkthrough covering validation, review, and observable acceptance
Small documentation patches deserve acceptance criteria that another agent can execute
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
